newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market steady, waits for clues.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market steady, waits for clues.

text.p: In calm Monday trade, Dutch money market rates stuck to the levels reached late on Friday afternoon.
Call money was quoted 3.06/12 at bid and was said to change hands around 3.125 percent.
Most deals were done in overnight money and short-term deposits up to three months, dealers said.
One dealer noted particular activity in one-week deposits, due to the ending of the Japanese fiscal year on March 31.
"They want one-week (deposits) to carry them into their new year and they pay the top for them," he said.

One-week deposits were quoted at up to 3.18/26 percent bid/ask. Dealers said that overall, trade on the money market was likely to remain calm if players were uncertain about the direction it would take in the near future.
One said the market was awaiting the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting due on Tuesday, while another said it looked at the Dutch and German official rates.
Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) were set at 3.13 percent for the May programme and 3.29 percent for the December programme, dealers said, unchanged from Friday's levels.
They said primary trade in DTCs was close to nil.
"The (Finance Ministry's) Agent collected quite a lot last week. Now it looks like it's back on the shelf again," one said.
